answers: The review round of 2026-10-30 (.legion/INFRA-750/review.json, decision changes_requested, 0 critical, 0 important, 2 minor). Both findings are in the code and both were driven here.

implementerProof.how: This round's whole diff is one commit, 73196dfca8cd, over the reviewed head 721792617475: the replaced-watch INFO line's wording, Start's doc, the test constant that reads the line, and the extraction of the freeze-and-wait sequence into freezeUntilBothClientsReportTheCut. Every test that reads either was re-run here. `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=2 -run 'TestAFailedFirstStartLogsItsErrorOnlyWhileItIsTheLiveWatch$' ./internal/kvwatch/`: both rows pass twice (ok 1.574s). `go test -run 'TestBothOfTheListenersNATSClientsReportASilentCutWithinSeconds$|TestASilentCutRewatchesTheCachesWithNoErrorLine$' ./cmd/listener/`: both pass (ok 12.042s), each printing the per-client timings the helper kept. `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=2 -run 'TestAHubThatStopsAnsweringIsNoticedWithinSeconds$' ./internal/natsauth/` from packages/daemon: 2 of 2 (ok 7.084s). Three negative controls, each a break of production with the tests untouched, go red. The earlier entries were verified at their own heads in rounds 1 and 2 and their code is untouched by this commit.

proof.criterion: Review finding 1 (minor, kvwatch.go:212): the replaced-watch line must name the failure as the first watch's own, not as something the rewatch caused, and Start's doc must say the real condition.
proof.surface: The kvwatch watcher against a real in-process NATS server, both branches driven through its public API, with the records read from a JSON logger; and the source the finding cites.
proof.observed: Both rows pass twice (ok 1.574s) with the line now reading `<cache> first watch failed after a rewatch replaced it; the replacement feeds the cache`, which the test's `replaced` constant matches. The finding's premise was checked in the code rather than taken: `watch` returns an error at two places only, `bus.ReadStreamState` (internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go:515) and `open` with `from == 0` (:525-527), both before any watcher is installed, so the new doc's `The watch fails only before it has installed a watcher, so the error is always the first watch's own` is true, and so is its `While no watcher is current` condition.
proof.negativeControl: Start's old body restored (the unconditional ERROR before the lock, `if !current { w.signalReady() }` after it), both test files untouched: `--- FAIL ... a first watch a rewatch replaced logged [test cache watch failed: nats: connection closed], want no ERROR`, while the `no replacement` row still passes. kvwatch.go was restored with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: Review finding 2 (minor, cut_rewatch_test.go:43-65): the freeze-and-wait-for-both-cut-lines sequence must live in one helper both listener tests call, keeping the per-client diagnostic and the timing log.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary with the live lane on, against an in-process NATS whose relay freezes; both tests that now call the helper.
proof.observed: Both pass (ok 12.042s). The timing log survived the extraction and is printed by both callers: `envoy reported the cut 2.799s after it began` and `envoy-live-topics ... 2.85s` from the cut test, `2.786s` and `2.836s` from the rewatch test. The helper takes its own log offset per call, so a caller that freezes twice judges each cut on its own window.
proof.negativeControl: The per-client diagnostic is still live after the extraction: `bus.WithSilentCutDetection()` removed from listenerStreamOptions alone, the test files untouched, fails naming one client only — `no disconnect line for envoy 5.025s into a silent cut`, with `envoy-live-topics`'s `nats: stale connection` line present. main.go was restored with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: The whole cut path of the real listener still writes no ERROR line, and a second cut in the same process ends as the first does.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary with its three caches and the live lane, frozen and thawed twice in one process, read through its own log and its GET /v1/interests/.
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `go test -run 'TestASilentCutRewatchesTheCachesWithNoErrorLine$' ./cmd/listener/`, and a throwaway two-cut test of the tester's own on the new helper (TestTwoSilentCutsInARowRewatchTheCachesWithNoErrorLine), run the same way and removed afterwards since it pins no defect.
proof.observed: The implementer's guard passes. The two-cut run passed in 11.08 s: cut 1 reported 2.835 s in by both clients and every one of the three caches warmed up again 1.064 s after the thaw; cut 2 reported 2.996 s in and every cache warmed up again 1.015 s after the thaw; an interest another listener wrote after the second thaw reached this listener's cache 103 ms later; and the process wrote no ERROR line at all, its start included.
proof.negativeControl: The guard's no-ERROR assertion is live at this head, after the output reader moved into the helper: one `slog.Error` added to rewatchListenerKVWatchers in cmd/listener/main.go, which the cut path runs, makes it fail — `a silent cut and its rewatch logged an error: ... ERROR tester control: rewatching a cache cache=interest`. main.go was restored with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: The two headline criteria still hold at this head: the listener reports a silent cut within 5 seconds, and the daemon reports one within the same bound.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary against a frozen relay, and the daemon's own natsauth.Connect against a server that answers the handshake and then nothing.
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestBothOfTheListenersNATSClientsReportASilentCutWithinSeconds$' ./cmd/listener/`. From packages/daemon: `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=2 -timeout 10m -v -run 'TestAHubThatStopsAnsweringIsNoticedWithinSeconds$' ./internal/natsauth/`.
proof.observed: The listener: pass, `envoy` 2.799 s and `envoy-live-topics` 2.85 s after the freeze; in the two-cut run both clients reported each of two cuts at 2.835 s and 2.996 s. The daemon: 2 of 2 under -race (ok 7.084s), the cut noticed 3.011111250 s and 3.016850422 s after the server went quiet.
proof.negativeControl: The listener control above (the option removed from listenerStreamOptions alone). For the daemon, the same break ran in rounds 1 and 2 — `options = append(options, detectSilentCuts)` removed from Connect gives `the connection was not reported lost within 5.0105s ...: IsConnected = true, the warning logged = false` — and packages/daemon is untouched by this round's commit, which the diff 721792617475..73196dfca8cd shows: it holds only internal/kvwatch and cmd/listener test files.

ciAtTheHead: The code head 73196dfca8cd carries CI run 41026772876, queued at 08:34Z with `changes` queued and `pr-title` queued; the handoff head ac614cc1 carries none, which is right, since its push touched `.legion/INFRA-750/` alone and its message carries `skip-checks: true`, so the daemon carries the code head's verdict to it. Round 2's run at b41bf83f reads `cancelled` throughout: the newer push superseded it under ci.yaml's `cancel-in-progress` for a pull request. A queued lane is read as queued; nothing here waited for it and no lane was re-run as evidence.
environment: Every test in this handoff runs against an in-process NATS server from internal/testnats; no container and no external server is needed, and none was left running.

This pod has no container runtime, so the cmd/listener tests that start a Postgres container and the three natsauth tests that need an authorized-server container do not run here, as the implementer records. CI runs them.
alsoChecked: The helper's contract: it returns the thaw and the output reader, takes a fresh log offset at each call, and registers its own `t.Cleanup(thaw)`; the freeze is a `sync.OnceFunc`, so a caller that thaws and the cleanup that thaws again are safe, which the two-cut run exercises twice.

The review's two findings are the whole of this round's diff. Nothing else of the pull request changed: `jj diff -r '721792617475::73196dfca8cd' --stat` lists internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go, internal/kvwatch/kvwatch_test.go, cmd/listener/silent_cut_test.go, cmd/listener/cut_rewatch_test.go and the two handoff files.
The new text names no Dispatch key: every added line outside .legion/INFRA-750/ holds no INFRA-, LEGION- or dispatch:// text.

One prose nit the reviewer may want to take itself, not a failure and not a defect: the unit test's name, TestAFailedFirstStartLogsItsErrorOnlyWhileItIsTheLiveWatch, keeps the wording the finding corrected in the doc (`while it is still the live one`). The meaning is right — the first watch is the live watch exactly while no replacement is current — but the doc now says `While no watcher is current` and the name does not.
